the model says the meaning changed: Refusals whose reason is in NO_HISTORY no longer open a debug case, which weakens "a step refuses what a requirement says it handles → one debug case", and nothing shown says this exclusion is allowed.; brought to the owner as a card: The requirement still matches what you asked for. You want plumb to open a debug case right away whenever one of its steps refuses something it should handle. The requirement says the same: when the repin step refuses a link, one debug case is written and you are asked nothing.

The change adds an exception to the turn-end stale check. Until now, every refusal opened a debug case unless the refusal was because no model was available. Now refusals whose reason is a "no history" reason also open no case.

What I can't tell is whether those refusals are plumb failing. If "no history" means plumb has no earlier version to compare against, the step may be right to refuse, and skipping the case is just cleanup. If it means plumb lost or never wrote history it should have, then hiding it breaks the rule that every refusal of something plumb should handle gets a debug case. The prompt from the turn that probably made this change was about the workflow tool in the build step. It didn't ask for this exception, and nothing on record allows it.; the card is not offered until it is complete, it lacks: what option 1 ("Keep the change: a refusal for missing history is not a plumb failure, and the requirement is reworded to say so") does and leaves undone; what option 2 ("Undo the change: every refusal from the stale check except 'no model available' opens a debug case") does and leaves undone; what option 3 ("Keep skipping the case, but only once it is confirmed that missing history can never come from a plumb bug; otherwise open a case") does and leaves undone; why the recommended option is recommended (plumb stale card SR-325#7 --consequences "..." --why "...")
